comments.content: The skip tag is persisted eagerly, before the install is even attempted, and nothing rolls it back if the install never happens. `installAsset` can abort after this point — package-name mismatch (`ApkValidationResult.PackageMismatch`), the signing-key warning path that returns early, a cancelled/failed download, or the user leaving the screen — while `skippedReleaseTag` stays set. In those cases the user is still on the newer build but the release they never moved away from is silently suppressed (no update CTA, plus a "skipped" badge in the apps list) until they unskip it manually. Additionally, the write runs in a detached coroutine, so it is not guaranteed to have landed before the install pipeline's `updateAppVersion` reads `skippedReleaseTag` to recompute `isUpdateAvailable` (a parked-file install can reach that write quickly). Consider persisting the skip only once the downgrade has actually been recorded (e.g. alongside the successful `saveInstalledAppToDatabase`/`updateAppVersion` outcome), or reverting it when the install does not complete.

comments.content:
Suppressing the flag here leaves a self-inconsistent record that later corrupts `installedVersion`.

After a skipped/downgraded install, this copy keeps `latestVersion` = the newer skipped tag, but line 471 then overwrites `latestVersionCode` with `newVersionCode`, i.e. the code of the just-installed (older) build. So the row becomes: `latestVersion = v4.0`, `latestVersionCode = N2`, `installedVersion = v2.0`, `installedVersionCode = N2`.

On the very next `checkForUpdates`, `codesAlreadyMatch` evaluates true (`installedCode == latestCode` and `matchedRelease.tagName == app.latestVersion`, both N2 / v4.0), which makes the reconciliation block at lines 377-387 run `updateInstalledVersion(installedVersion = matchedRelease.tagName)`. The device is actually running v2.0, yet the app is recorded as v4.0 (and `SmartInstallButton` then shows the "installed" state for v4.0), so the skip silently turns into a misreported installed version instead of just a suppressed update.

Suggestion: when `snapshotIsSkipped` is true, keep the version-code pair aligned with `latestVersion` (preserve `app.latestVersionCode` instead of `newVersionCode`), or clear `latestVersion`/`latestVersionCode` together so `codesAlreadyMatch` cannot misfire.
